method.sample: Same frozen-engine historical cohort and exact initial-hash/full-seed pairing as VP pilot.
method.currentOutcome: T1-4 same outcome; VP uses T4 control margin; supply uses early mean burden.
method.targets: Final cumulative events, final VP margin, and T5-end mean supply burden. Candidate minus same-side self-play.
method.countProjection: Early cumulative count difference multiplied by 8/4; no multiplier for VP or mean supply burden.
method.ridge: Unpenalized intercept and current-outcome slope, added coefficients lambda=1; train-only preprocessing.
method.bootstrap: 1000 seed-cluster resamples of fixed CV errors; conditional intervals omit fitting and selection uncertainty.

limitations: All data are previously inspected development games, not prospective validation.
Three related assault variants and ten seeds; all three attacker mean VP changes are negative.
Defender j/q variants share behavior; defender results remain descriptive.
Multiple outcomes and features are explored without multiplicity correction or nested selection.
Enemy loss events include attrition; they do not establish kills caused by our policy.
Fixed initial RE denominators do not prevent destruction from reducing later supply demand.
Joint gap is the existing priority allocator unallocated demand, not an optimal allocation or causal effect.
Each condition is added separately to the early-outcome baseline; this does not test joint allocation conditional on individual access.
